name: Mei
tagline: An assistant built into the GNOME desktop that does things, not only chats
description: Mei is a GNOME Shell 50 extension and a Python runtime that together act as an everyday desktop assistant. You ask from the top bar, a shortcut, or by voice; Mei plans, uses 34 tools (files, apps and windows, desktop settings, sandboxed commands, memory, the clipboard, media, and the screen through accessibility), and asks in plain words before anything that changes your computer. It works with local models (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio) and cloud APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, OpenCode, GitHub Models, any OpenAI-compatible URL). Voice runs on the computer: wake word, Live conversation with barge-in, dictation and read-aloud. Keys stay in the keyring; content from files and pages is treated as data, never as instructions.
highlights: A durable agent loop: every action is recorded before it runs, so a crash or a Shell restart resumes or asks, never repeats a change blindly
A policy engine decides per action whether to ask: approvals in Mei's own words, task and standing grants, and floors no grant can lift (startup folders, data leaving the machine)
Content Mei reads (files, PDFs, the clipboard, the screen) taints the task, so a document can't steer Mei into changes or plant memories the person didn't confirm
Sandboxed commands run in bubblewrap on descriptor-pinned folders, with secret files masked and watched while they run
Local voice with sherpa-onnx: wake word, streaming speech-to-text, Piper and Kokoro speech, echo-cancelled barge-in, and a Live bar that follows who is speaking
Computer use through AT-SPI and the ScreenCast portal: forms, buttons and text through accessibility first, a password hand-off, and a kill switch the Shell enforces
779 runtime tests, about 100 extension tests, 28 scored agent evals, and end-to-end runs in nested GNOME Shells that never touch the real session
44 decision records document each design choice and what superseded it

story.why: A desktop assistant in the spirit of Gemini on Android: one that understands intent and finishes everyday tasks on the computer, not a coding tool or a chat window.
story.problem: Chat assistants can talk about your computer but can't safely act on it. Acting needs durable state, honest approvals, protection against instructions hidden in content, and privacy for what local models see.
challenges: Shell code can't block or crash, so the agent, tools and voice run in a separate Python runtime reached over D-Bus (runtime/src/mei/ipc)
A file or page can carry instructions for the assistant; taint and provenance tracking keep it from turning into actions or memories (runtime/src/mei/policy, core/remember.py)
Commands and file changes must act on what was judged, not on a path that a link swap redirected (capabilities/fs_at.py, desktop/sandbox.py)
Voice has to be fast on a CPU, pause for other apps that record, and never hear itself through the speakers (runtime/src/mei/voice)
Acting on other apps' windows through accessibility, with the person able to stop it at once even if the runtime freezes (runtime/src/mei/computer)
designDecisions: The extension is UI only; the runtime owns the agent loop, the store and every tool (docs/decisions)
Every action is written to SQLite before it runs and its result before the next model call, so recovery never guesses (runtime/src/mei/core/loop.py)
One policy engine with presets and grants decides each action; some floors ask every time whatever was granted (runtime/src/mei/policy/engine.py)
What a local model wrote stays off cloud models, and local-only memories never leave (runtime/src/mei/core/context.py)
Voice runs in a jailed worker process speaking a small versioned wire protocol (runtime/src/mei/voice/wire.py)
Tests never touch the real desktop: private homes, buses, PipeWire and nested headless Shells (scripts/e2e-stage1.sh, scripts/e2e-computer.sh)

future.next: Exact context limits per model, learned from the provider and from overflow errors, so long tasks fit any model.
roadmap: Per-model context limits and Ollama context sizing
Text that carries where it came from, replacing the interim rule that keeps a local model's words off cloud models
Broader computer use: browsers and more apps through accessibility
